steps.title: Confirm the Year 1 commissioning briefs and delivery rhythm
steps.summary: Turn the agreed Year 1 portfolio into four clear commissioning briefs, confirm named ownership where still TBC, and establish the shared annual rhythm. All four packages run across the academic year: autumn emphasises scalable and low-friction entry, spring increases active and sustained engagement, and post-exam and summer periods create more space for intensive provision where appropriate. The Belonging and Connection package remains predominantly short and active throughout. Each brief uses the same planning frame of investment, unique reach, engagement depth, delivery mix and student-hours.

outputs.title: Year 1 commissioning briefs and shared delivery rhythm
outputs.summary: Four distinct briefs for the Final-Year Career Enhancement Programme, Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience Programme, Belonging and Connection Programme, and Service and Community-Engaged Experience Programme. Each brief preserves the common commissioning principle that investment should create substantive skills or experiential value rather than awareness alone, while responsiveness to emerging evidence and priorities remains a feature of the portfolio as a whole.

decisions.title: Confirm named Careers owner for the Final-Year Career Enhancement Programme
decisions.summary: Confirm the accountable programme owner within Careers and Employability before substantive commissioning begins.

decisions.title: Confirm owner for the Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience Programme
decisions.summary: Confirm the accountable programme owner for the entrepreneurship and enterprise commissioning package before substantive commissioning begins.

steps.title: Run the Final-Year Career Enhancement Programme
steps.summary: Run a year-round package of substantive career-enhancing skills and experience for students approaching graduation. Prioritise programmes and student groups where additional intervention is most likely to add value, drawing on course-level graduate outcomes, demographic intersections, career-readiness self-report and evidence of prior employability engagement. Use scalable and short active provision throughout the year while protecting a meaningful sustained high-intensity layer through projects, placements, mentoring and other deeper experiences.

outputs.title: Final-Year Career Enhancement Programme
outputs.owner: Careers and Employability Service, named owner TBC
outputs.summary: A £50,000 commissioned programme engaging around 10% of the graduating undergraduate population, circa 700 unique students, through approximately 10,000 to 12,000 student-hours of activity. Around 150 students access sustained high-intensity provision. The offer focuses on skills and experiences students can practise, demonstrate or carry forward rather than awareness-raising alone.

newInvestment.item: Final-Year Career Enhancement Programme commissioning envelope
newInvestment.rationale: Funds a balanced year-round portfolio of scalable, active and sustained career-enhancing opportunities for final-year undergraduates, protecting intensive provision for around 150 students while maintaining reach to approximately 10% of the graduating undergraduate population.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The programme cannot create the intended scale and depth of additional career-enhancing skills and experiential provision for students approaching graduation.

steps.title: Run the Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience Programme
steps.summary: Run a year-round entrepreneurship and enterprise programme with a broad practical funnel into deeper entrepreneurial experience. Use scalable provision to build accessible enterprise capability, short active formats for challenge, idea development, prototyping and hackathon-style activity, and a sustained layer for venture-building, social enterprise, live briefs, incubation-style work and longer enterprise projects. The emphasis is on students practising entrepreneurial behaviours and producing or testing something rather than simply learning about entrepreneurship.

outputs.title: Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience Programme
outputs.summary: A £40,000 commissioned programme aiming to engage approximately 800 unique students through around 7,000 to 9,000 student-hours. Around 100 students access sustained high-intensity entrepreneurial experience, supported by a broader mix of scalable and short active enterprise provision.

newInvestment.item: Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience Programme commissioning envelope
newInvestment.rationale: Funds a year-round entrepreneurship and enterprise pathway combining broad practical reach with challenge-based activity and sustained venture-building or enterprise experiences for around 100 students.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: King's will have less capacity to create accessible, substantive entrepreneurial experience beyond the course and to provide a deeper pathway for students ready to develop ideas, ventures or enterprise capability.

steps.title: Run the Belonging and Connection Programme
steps.summary: Run a high-volume, year-round programme of frequent, low-friction opportunities for connection, participation and wellbeing, responding directly to 2.3.2 Belonging and Participation: Physical and Digital and 2.3.4 Rhythms of the Academic Year and Student Experience. The programme is predominantly made up of active one- and two-hour experiences, punctuated by a smaller number of larger sandpit-style events. Repeat participation is encouraged where it strengthens connection and belonging, and is tracked separately from unique reach.

outputs.title: Belonging and Connection Programme
outputs.summary: A £30,000 high-reach programme working towards approximately 1,500 unique students and around 1,800 participation instances, generating approximately 3,500 to 4,500 student-hours through a broad scatter of short active opportunities and a smaller number of deeper participatory or sandpit-style experiences across the academic year.

newInvestment.item: Belonging and Connection Programme commissioning envelope
newInvestment.rationale: Funds a lean, high-volume programme of active participation opportunities and selected deeper or sandpit-style experiences, using existing spaces and infrastructure wherever possible to maximise reach while supporting repeat engagement.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The concrete opportunity asks generated through the belonging, participation and academic-year-rhythm work will have limited commissioning capacity behind them.

steps.title: Run the Service and Community-Engaged Experience Programme
steps.summary: Run a year-round programme that mobilises King's service and external engagement agenda through meaningful community-engaged activity. Commission opportunities in which service and contribution are also deliberate routes to skills development, experience, networks and graduate advantage. Use accessible community-engaged entry points and short active projects alongside a protected sustained layer of deeper projects, placements or partner-based experiences, concentrating intensive activity where the academic calendar and partner capacity make deeper engagement possible.

outputs.title: Service and Community-Engaged Experience Programme
outputs.summary: A £30,000 commissioned year-round programme aiming to engage approximately 600 unique students through around 6,000 to 8,000 student-hours of substantive community-engaged experience. Around 100 students access sustained high-intensity projects, placements or comparable deeper experiences.

newInvestment.item: Service and Community-Engaged Experience Programme commissioning envelope
newInvestment.rationale: Funds community-engaged opportunities that combine service and contribution with substantive skills and employment-enhancing experience, including sustained high-intensity provision for around 100 students.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: King's will have less capacity to turn its service agenda into accessible developmental experience beyond the course and to protect deeper community-engaged opportunities.

steps.title: Complete and review the Year 1 commissioning portfolio
steps.summary: Close the first annual commissioning cycle against a clear portfolio-level reach commitment, then review the year as a portfolio rather than as four isolated programmes. Deduplicate reach across packages, examine student-hours and repeat engagement where relevant, review the balance of scalable, active and intensive provision, assess delivery quality and access, and identify where demand or strategic need remains unmet. The four package-level reach ambitions sum to approximately 3,600 students before cross-package deduplication, with approximately 26,500 to 33,500 student-hours planned and around 350 sustained high-intensity places across the Final-Year Career Enhancement, Entrepreneurship and Enterprise, and Service and Community-Engaged packages, alongside the deeper active layer in Belonging and Connection. Use this evidence alongside the maturing feeder projects to decide what should grow, reshape, stop or be newly commissioned in Year 2.

outputs.title: Year 1 portfolio reach and engagement
outputs.summary: At least 2,500 unique students engage in substantive beyond-course opportunities through the Year 1 commissioning portfolio, counted once at portfolio level even where they participate in more than one package. Package-level planning anticipates approximately 26,500 to 33,500 student-hours overall; this depth measure is reviewed alongside repeat participation and delivery mix rather than used to inflate unique reach.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 2,500 unique students are recorded across the Year 1 portfolio after deduplication between packages.

outputs.title: Year 1 portfolio review and Year 2 commissioning plan
outputs.summary: A concise evidence-led review of reach, repeat participation, student-hours, delivery mix, access and unmet demand, with recommendations for what should grow, reshape, stop or be newly commissioned in the next annual portfolio.
